title: SS-VIME: Single-Source Virome-Microbiome Extraction Protocol
author: Abdonaser Poursalavati
materials: Important Note : The dsRNA concentration will be measured using a high-sensitivity dsDNA Qubit (unofficially confirmed in discussions with Thermo Fisher's Qubit team). After column chromatography and digestion with RNase and DNase, we expect minimal to no RNA and variable amounts of DNA (theoretically dsRNA), typically reading below 2 ng/µl for soil samples.

Important Note : The dsRNA concentration will be measured using a high-sensitivity dsDNA Qubit (unofficially confirmed in discussions with Thermo Fisher's Qubit team). After column chromatography and digestion with RNase and DNase, we expect minimal to no RNA and variable amounts of DNA (theoretically dsRNA), typically reading below 2 ng/µl for soil samples.

steps.title: Sample Storage
steps.instruction: Immediately upon arrival, freeze soil samples at -80°C (or -20°C for storage durations under 6 months).

steps.title: Prepare Bead Tubes
steps.instruction: Prepare silica bead tubes in advance and store at -20°C.

substeps.instruction: Autoclave 0.1 mm and 3 mm silica beads separately.
Under a laminar flow hood, transfer 2 ml of 0.1 mm beads and 10 of the 3 mm beads into 15 ml tubes.
Store the prepared bead tubes at -20°C.

steps.title: Weigh Soil Samples
steps.instruction: Weigh soil samples and transfer them to pre-frozen bead tubes (cooled at -20°C for at least 2 hours).

substeps.instruction: Remove stones or debris using a sterilized toothpick or spatula.
Weigh 1.5 - 2 grams of mineral soil, or 1 - 1.5 grams of organic or peat soil, adjusting for texture and large particles.

steps.title: Prepare Equipment and Buffers
steps.instruction: Set up the necessary buffers and laboratory equipment.

substeps.instruction: Prepare a fresh batch of chromatography washing buffer.
Heat a water bath to 37°C.
Set the centrifuge with a 15 ml bucket to 4°C and place the 5 ml rotor in the refrigerator to reach 4°C.
Fill a Styrofoam container with ice.

steps.title: Prepare Cellulose Slurry
steps.instruction: Create a cellulose slurry for column preparation.

substeps.instruction: Combine 1.6 grams of Sigma cellulose powder with 16 ml of chromatography washing buffer.
Shake the mixture for 15 minutes at 300 rpm.
Centrifuge the slurry at 2500 rpm for 1 minute and discard the supernatant.
Add another 16 ml washing buffer and shake for 10 minutes at 300 rpm.

steps.title: Add Lysis Reagents
steps.instruction: Add the following reagents to each frozen bead tube containing soil:

substeps.instruction: 4 ml of PVP-amended CTAB buffer
100 μl of β-mercaptoethanol
2 ml of water-saturated phenol (pH 6.5) and 2 ml of chloroform – isoamyl alcohol (24:1) [Alternatively: 4 ml of PCI mixture 25:24:1]

steps.title: Seal and Homogenize
steps.instruction: Seal tubes with Parafilm (if caps lack built-in seals) and homogenize using a MiniG homogenizer at 1500 rpm.

substeps.instruction: Standard soil: Homogenize for 1.5 minutes, pausing for 1 minute on ice every 30 seconds.
Organic/peat soil: Start with two rounds of 15 seconds each, with 1 minute of cooling in between; increase up to 1.5 minutes if yield is insufficient.

steps.title: Vortex and Rest
steps.instruction: Perform a series of high-speed vortexing and resting steps.

substeps.instruction: Cool for 1 minute, then vortex at high speed for 1 minute, 2 minutes, and 5 minutes, with 1-minute cooling intervals between each (For organic/peat soil, reduce the final vortex to 2 minutes and ensure speed does not exceed 1500 rpm).
Allow tubes to rest on the vortex for 10 minutes.
Perform a final 1-minute high-speed vortex.

steps.title: Centrifuge Lysing Tubes
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the lysing tubes at 5000 rpm for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Prepare Cellulose Columns
steps.instruction: Prepare Pierce centrifuge columns using the slurry.

substeps.instruction: Transfer 2 ml of slurry to 2 ml Pierce centrifuge columns.
Perform a pulse spin for 30 seconds and discard the liquids.

steps.title: Load and Shake Columns
steps.instruction: Load the aqueous phase and ethanol into the columns and shake.

substeps.instruction: Add 3 ml of the lysing tubes' aqueous phase to each column.
Add 580 μl of anhydrous ethanol to each column (final concentration ~16.2%).
Seal both ends of the columns and shake thoroughly for 10 minutes at 200 rpm, periodically rotating the columns.

steps.title: Collect Total DNA
steps.instruction: Collect the initial liquid for total DNA analysis.

substeps.instruction: Loosen the cap, place the column in a fresh 15 ml tube, and pulse spin for 30 seconds.
Collect all liquid into a screw-capped 5 ml tube and store at -20°C.

steps.title: Wash Columns
steps.instruction: Wash the columns to remove remaining materials.

substeps.instruction: Add 2 ml of chromatography washing buffer, briefly shake or vortex, and incubate for 1 minute.
Transfer the column to a 15 ml tube and pulse spin for 30 seconds.
Discard the liquid (or save for RNA analysis if required).
Dry the columns by performing a 30-second pulse spin with the cap open.

steps.title: Elute dsRNA
steps.instruction: Elute the dsRNA from the columns.

substeps.instruction: Add 2 ml of pure water, gently shake, and incubate for 2 minutes.
Place each column into a new 15 ml tube.
Optional: Transfer any pelleted cellulose from the 15 ml tube back to the column.
Perform a 30-second pulse spin and transfer the liquid to a screw-capped 5 ml tube.

steps.title: Enzymatic Treatment
steps.instruction: Treat the dsRNA eluate with enzymes to remove DNA and single-stranded RNA.

substeps.instruction: Add 195-200 μl of 10x DNase buffer to each 5 ml eluted tube.
Add 3 μl of DNase I (1 U/μl) and 5 μl of RNase T1 (10 U/μl).
Hand shake for 15 seconds and incubate at 37°C for 30 minutes in a water bath.

steps.title: PCI Extraction and Purification
steps.instruction: Purify the dsRNA and DNA fractions using PCI and chloroform.

substeps.instruction: Add 2 ml of PCI to the enzyme-treated tubes, hand shake for 15 seconds, and centrifuge at 18,000 G for 10 minutes.
Thaw DNA tubes from -20°C completely.
Transfer 2 aliquots of ~950 μl from each PCI tube into new screw-capped 5 ml tubes.
Add an equal volume of chloroform to all DNA, dsRNA, and RNA tubes, hand shake for 15 seconds, and centrifuge at 18,000 G for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Aqueous Phase Transfer
steps.instruction: Carefully transfer the aqueous phases to new Eppendorf tubes.

substeps.instruction: Transfer two aliquots of 830 μl from the dsRNA portion (~1.7 ml total) into a 5 ml Eppendorf tube.
Combine three aliquots of 835 μl from the DNA portion (~2.5 ml total) into another Eppendorf tube using a P1000 pipette.
Avoid contact with the interphase.

steps.title: Precipitate Nucleic Acids
steps.instruction: Precipitate the DNA and dsRNA using PEG-NaCl.

substeps.instruction: Add an equal volume of PEG-NaCl to each tube, close the cap, and hand-shake for 15 seconds.
Incubate on ice for at least 25 minutes (recommended 55 minutes to 1 hour); store in the fridge at 4°C if possible.
Centrifuge at 18,000 G for 15 minutes.
Pour off supernatant and use a P1000 pipette to remove remaining liquid while keeping the tube inverted, avoiding the pellet.

steps.title: Wash and Dry Pellets
steps.instruction: Wash the pellets with ethanol and air-dry.

substeps.instruction: Add 2 ml of 75% cold ethanol, close the cap, and hand shake thoroughly.
Centrifuge at 18,000 G for 10 minutes.
Immediately pour off ethanol and air-dry the pellet for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Final Elution
steps.instruction: Elute the purified DNA and dsRNA into PCR tubes.

substeps.instruction: Elute the DNA pellet using 50 μl of TE buffer.
Elute the dsRNA pellet using 30 μl of TE buffer.
If the solution is cloudy or contains cellulose, perform a high-speed spin and transfer the clarified solution to new PCR tubes.

steps.title: Quality Control
steps.instruction: Quantify and verify the extracted nucleic acids.

substeps.instruction: Perform Nanodrop analysis using 2 μl for each component (optionally use Qubit).
Run a 0.7-1% agarose gel to verify extraction quality.

description: Important Notes: This protocol is optimized for processing up to 8 samples in parallel, which is the recommended maximum. The procedure will yield 16 final outputs (DNA and dsRNA) and can be completed in under 8 hours.
